title: pm-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-28
content:
Daily scratchpad - Maya R. - 2026-03-28

Top priorities for today:
- Finalize PRD edits for adaptive-batching (see confluence:PRD-adaptive-batching-6089). Need decision on default batch timeout and max batch size.
- Sync with SRE about canary infra for Dedicated (E2E smoke infra + rollback hooks). Meeting 11:00.
- Follow up with Eng (Kara) on quantized model perf regression (reported by QA on 3/26). Ticket INF-2345 assigned.
- Draft launch checklist for internal rollout to beta customers (aiming 4/12).

Notes / PRD edits (quick):
- Problem statement: variable request sizes + tail latency spikes -> want adaptive batching to smooth throughput while keeping 99th latency within SLA.
- Proposed approach: dynamic batching window with latency SLO feedback + prioritized small requests bypass when necessary.
- Config knobs (needs simple defaults):
  - batch_timeout_ms: 10 (candidate), 5 (low-latency mode)
  - max_batch_tokens: 2048
  - max_batch_count: 32
  - priority_threshold_tokens: 64 (requests under this considered priority)
- Acceptance criteria (must be measurable):
  - 95th token latency improvement >= 15% on mixed workload vs current static batching
  - No more than 5% increase in cost-per-token for steady-state workloads
  - No regression on long-context throughput (>1024 tokens)
- Open question: do we expose batch_timeout_ms to customers or keep it internal and surface only mode presets (low-latency / balanced / throughput)? My leaning: presets for simplicity, expose advanced knob in Dedicated/Private.

Action items (owners):
- Kara (eng-serving-runtime): run perf suite with quantized model + adaptive-batching branch (PR #4521) by 3/30. Capture 50k request sample, mix distributions in perf harness.
- Ethan (SRE): confirm canary routing plan + rollback playbook; confirm metrics surfaced in Console (per-route latency buckets). Due 4/1.
- Priya (PM): draft customer-facing one-pager for beta program and send to TPB. Due 4/2.
- QA (TBD): create smoke tests for batch correctness (ordering, tokenization boundary cases).

Meeting notes (standup snippets):
- 09:30 standup: Kara flagged a likely off-by-one in KV cache concat that breaks very small batched requests. Quick patch planned; impact limited.
- 10:15 sync with analytics: need new telemetry events: batching.window_ms, batch.size_tokens, batch.request_count, batch.priority_flag. Add to tracing schema and Console dashboard.

Launch checklist (draft):
- Docs:
  - PRD updated & linked -> confluence:PRD-adaptive-batching-6089 (done, WG review pending)
  - Internal playbook for rollback (SRE) -> link TBD
  - Customer one-pager + FAQ (product) -> draft by 4/2
- Testing:
  - Unit + integration tests for batching logic (eng) -> PR passing CI
  - Perf benchmarks: compare baseline vs adaptive on Hosted/Dedicated/Private (appliances) -> target 4/6
  - End-to-end smoke tests in canary -> pass for 48h before wider rollout
- Observability:
  - Console metrics tracked (latency buckets, cost per token, error rate) -> panels created by Observability team
  - Alerts: spike in 99th latency, increased error rate post-deploy -> default thresholds set
- Rollout plan:
  - Canary: 1% traffic for 24h -> 5% 24h -> 25% 48h -> 100%
  - Auto rollback triggers: 99th latency increase >25% OR error rate >0.5% sustained 15m
- Stakeholders to notify:
  - Customer success (beta contacts), Sales AE on accounts with Dedicated, Support readiness email

Risks / open items:
- Perf regressions on quantized checkpoints (blocked on Kara's perf runs).
- Complexity in exposing advanced knobs may increase support burden - need doc + runbook.
- Decision required on UI surface for presets vs knobs (product + UX).

Quick wins / notes to self:
- Add example k6 load script to perf repo for replaying mixed workloads (will copy from INF-perf/scripts).
- Reuse metrics panels from reranking launch as template.

Slack / links to follow up:
- Slack thread: #prod-release "adaptive batching rollout" (pinned notes)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4521 (adaptive-batching branch)
- Jira: INF-2345 (quantized perf regression)
- Confluence: PRD-adaptive-batching-6089

End-of-day quick retrospective:
- What went well: PRD first pass feels much clearer after Kara + Ethan sync.
- Blockers: need perf numbers to lock defaults.
- Tomorrow: review Kara's perf outputs, update acceptance criteria if needed, finalize canary infra with Ethan.

Misc scratch notes (brain dump):
- Consider adding simulated small-request bypass path to reduce p99 on chat workloads where user messages often <64 tokens.
- Check license implications for third-party quant libs (if used in Private).
- Reminder: prep agenda for 4/1 all-hands on Dedicated infra updates (5 slides).
